whole_clause_reasoning.syntax: The complete rename-failure example establishes the matrix sequence: negative plus possibility, infinitival action, past negative predicate, then action object. The independent memory example establishes the complete completion-plus-current-operation complement. The candidate retains that nominal/infinitival action form intact and places it in the attested action slot, with its object in the attested post-predicate object slot. This is productive syntactic adaptation, not a claim that two arbitrary vocabulary matches alone certify a sentence.
whole_clause_reasoning.temporal_fit: The outer predicate is the explicit past-failure form from the complete could-not example, not the bare cannot/could-not column fragment or a silently repaired glyph. The inner completion form remains nonfinite; no unsupported new tense conjugation is invented. This conveys failed completion of the requested action, matching the source.
whole_clause_reasoning.actor_fit: The matrix construction is interpreted as past nonpossibility of completing this operation. No explicit new user, team, first-person or other human actor is added. The completion form is the same general nonfinite form from the source operation example. The English we in the different rename example is not independently transferred into the candidate. This neutral event reading fits all nine callers.
whole_clause_reasoning.object_fit: The completion/action-object pairing is directly supported in software-operation context. This operation is a deictic rendering of the source the operation in the immediately current failed-action setting. It is not narrowed to drawing, editing pixels, files, memory exhaustion or a human task.
whole_clause_reasoning.glyph_and_punctuation: Attested syllabary sequences, including finalᎢ on the completion form, remain intact. Final period matches source. No new placeholder or Latin glyph repair. No visual glyph certification is claimed.
whole_clause_reasoning.scope: No memory cause, retry instruction, state-retention guarantee, successful rollback or data-loss claim is introduced. A failure to complete need not mean the operation performed no partial work.
